nodes.name: MIL-53 growth on NF
nodes.procedure: Self-supported Fe-based metal–organic framework (MOF) MIL-53 nanosheet arrays were grown onto pre-cleansed NF sheets via solvothermal reactions in the mixed solution of Fe^3+ and terephthalic acid (TPA) in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). Successful formation of MIL-53 on the NF surface was confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) and Raman spectroscopy.
nodes.source_text: Initially, self-supported Fe-based metal–organic framework (MOF) MIL-53 nanosheet arrays were grown onto pre-cleansed NF sheets via solvothermal reactions in the mixed solution of Fe^3+ and terephthalic acid (TPA) in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF).

nodes.name: Secondary hydrothermal CeO2 formation
nodes.procedure: The MOF precursors were subjected to a secondary hydrothermal treatment in Ce^3+-containing solution to obtain Fe2O3@CeO2 nanoheterojunction electrodes with nanoflower-like morphology. Through the Ce-assisted templated hydrolysis of the MOF precursor during the secondary hydrothermal reaction, the nanosheet arrays of MIL-53 transformed into self-assembled nanoflower structures.
nodes.source_text: The MOF precursors were subjected to a secondary hydrothermal treatment in Ce^3+-containing solution to obtain Fe2O3@CeO2 nanoheterojunction electrodes...

nodes.name: Oxygen vacancy engineering
nodes.procedure: Fe2O3@CeO2 nanoheterojunction electrodes were further annealed in an argon atmosphere to acquire defect-engineered Fe2O3@CeO2–Ov electrodes.
nodes.source_text: ...which were further annealed in an argon atmosphere to acquire defect-engineered Fe2O3@CeO2–Ov electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show Fe2O3 (JCPDS: 33-0644) and CeO2 (JCPDS: 34-0394) phases coexist; weak Fe2O3 peaks due to low crystallinity and amorphization; further weakening after annealing due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the secondary hydrothermal treatment, the peaks of MIL-53 disappeared, replaced by the peaks of Fe₂O₃ (JCPDS: 33-0644) and CeO₂ (JCPDS: 34-0394)... The weak diffraction intensities of Fe₂O₃ peaks might be due to the low crystallinity... signals from Fe₂O₃ further weakened after annealing, due to the introduction of additional oxygen vacancies

nodes.evidence_snippet: The hydrangea-like nanoflower microstructures with the scale around 1.5-3 μm comprised thin nanosheets with a thickness around 13 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: Ultrafine CeO2 nanocrystals below 10 nm distributed on Fe2O3 nanosheets; lattice fringes show 0.27 nm (104) plane of Fe2O3 and 0.31 nm (111) plane of CeO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the TEM images... numerous ultrafine nanocrystals with sizes below 10 nm are randomly distributed on the intergrown nanosheets. A high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image... shows obvious lattice fringes... 0.27 nm spacing are ascribed to the (104) plane of Fe₂O₃, and the (111) plane of CeO₂ with an interplanar distance of 0.31 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe and O homogeneously distributed; Ce located as randomly distributed high-concentration discrete islands confirming nanoparticle feature of CeO2 phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the heterogeneous Fe₂O₃@CeO₂... Fe and O are also homogeneously distributed throughout the materials, while Ce is located as randomly distributed high-concentration discrete islands

nodes.characterization_summary: Strongest magnetic signals at g=2.003 for Fe2O3@CeO2–OV indicate highest concentration of unpaired electrons induced by oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Formation of abundant oxygen vacancies was more directly confirmed by EPR as shown in Fig. 1i, where the strongest magnetic signals at g=2.003 for Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ indicated the highest concentration of unpaired electrons

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s: M-O (529.6 eV), M-OH (531.7 eV), H2O (533.5 eV); weakened M-O/strengthened M-OH ratio indicates abundant oxygen vacancies in Fe2O3@CeO2-OV; Ce 3d shows Ce3+ (882.3, 886.1, 900.5, 907.4, 904.9 eV) and Ce4+ peaks; Fe 2p shows Fe2+ (711.2/724.3 eV) and Fe0 (707 eV) confirming charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution O 1s spectrum of Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ shows... M–O (529.6 eV), M–OH (531.7 eV) and adsorbed H₂O (533.5 eV)... for Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ, the M–O signals are seriously weakened... Ce 3d spectrum... Ce³⁺ (green peaks at 882.3, 886.1, 900.5, 907.4 and 904.9 eV) and Ce⁴⁺... Fe 2p spectrum... Fe²⁺ (green peaks, 2p₃/₂ at 711.2 eV, 2p₁/₂ at 724.3 eV)... and Fe⁰ 2p³/₂ (707 eV)

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge: absorption edge shifts to lower energy indicating reduced Fe valence; Fe-O CN decreases to ~5.0, bond length expands from 1.99 Å to 2.07 Å; Ce L3-edge: white-line at lowest energy confirms increased Ce3+/Ce4+ ratio; Ce-O CN ~6.2 with extended 3.16 Å bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe K-edge XANES... defect-engineered Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ shows an obvious shift of the absorption edge to lower energy... Fe–O coordination number... decreases to ~5.0, with expanded Fe–O bond length from 1.99 Å to 2.07 Å... Ce L₃-edge XANES... white-line edge of Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ is located at the lowest energy... decreased first-shell Ce–O coordination number of ~6.2

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe2O3@CeO2–OV shows highest BET surface area of 75.44 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ shows the highest BET area of 75.44 m² g⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl calculated from CV at various scan rates: Fe2O3@CeO2-OV (31.2 mF/cm²), Fe2O3@CeO2 (27.3 mF/cm²), Fe2O3 (12.1 mF/cm²), CeO2 (9.3 mF/cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cdl values were calculated from cyclic voltammetry (CV) scans... Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ has the highest Cdl value of 31.2 mF cm⁻² followed by Fe₂O₃@CeO₂ (27.3 mF cm⁻²), Fe₂O₃ (12.1 mF cm⁻²), and CeO₂ (9.3 mF cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: Rct values: Fe2O3@CeO2–OV = 10.66 Ω, Fe2O3@CeO2 = 13.09 Ω, Fe2O3 = 26.71 Ω, CeO2 = 49.72 Ω.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Nyquist plots... heterojunction Fe₂O₃@CeO₂ shows a charge-transfer resistance (Rct) of 13.09 Ω... defect-rich Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ presented the lowest Rct of 10.66 Ω

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2 F2g peak at ~464 cm⁻¹ broadens after heterojunction formation; significant blueshift after annealing indicates lattice expansion and decreased crystallinity due to oxygen vacancies; Fe2O3 bands at 221, 289, 406, 653 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the CeO₂ sample, a distinct Raman band is observed at ~464 cm⁻¹... Characteristic Raman bands of Fe₂O₃ are present at 221, 289, 406 and 653 cm⁻¹... after the annealing process, the Raman peaks show a significant blueshift for the defect-engineered Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ sample

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM at nanosheet-nanoparticle boundary shows lattice fringes of 0.27 nm (Fe2O3 (104)) and 0.31 nm (CeO2 (111)) confirming heterojunction formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Fig. 1g focusing on the boundary between the nanosheet and nanoparticle shows obvious lattice fringes of distinct orientations and spacings... 0.27 nm spacing are ascribed to the (104) plane of Fe₂O₃, and the (111) plane of CeO₂ with an interplanar distance of 0.31 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: PDF profiles resemble CeO2 more than Fe2O3; enhanced Ce-Ce/Ce-O and decreased O-O peaks in Fe2O3@CeO2-OV confirm oxygen vacancy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PDF profiles of Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ and Fe₂O₃@CeO₂ mostly resemble that of CeO₂... For Fe₂O₃@CeO₂–Oᵥ, the Ce–Ce and Ce–O peaks are enhanced, while the O–O peak intensity decreases... indicating the loss of lattice oxygen and formation of oxygen vacancies
